verses.1: As for those who are responsible for building temples, we know that they all possess knowledge. Knowledge is a natural attribute; love, on the other hand, is what truly builds things.
verses.2: If someone seems to know something, then he should still know it, as it’s necessary for him to know it.
verses.3: But if anyone truly loves the God, then he will be known by Him.
verses.4: Regarding the worship of idols, we know that there is no idol in the world at all. And we also know that no god exists, except for one God alone.
verses.5: And indeed, although there are so-called gods, whether in the heavens or on earth, yet there are many gods and many lords.
verses.6: But to us, there is one God, our Father, from whom all things come. And there is also one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom all things belong to us.
verses.7: But knowledge isn’t universal. Some people, due to their familiarity with the idol, will eat it as if it were an idol itself. Their sense of perception becomes weak and ineffective.
verses.8: But starvation will not satisfy us with God’s desires. For whether we eat too much or not enough, we will still suffer the same consequences.
verses.9: But don’t let this mean that your power will be given to the weak.
verses.10: For if anyone were to see that person in a temple, it does not mean that his consciousness will be weakened or diminished as a result of being in such a place.
verses.11: For the sick man is restored to his original state of knowledge, through the brother whom Christ died for.
verses.12: In this way, then, you sin against your brothers, and by causing them to lose their unity with one another, you weaken their faith in Christ.
verses.13: Therefore, if my brother causes trouble for me, I won’t eat meat during the season when it’s not suitable to do so. This is so that I won’t cause trouble for my brother.
